trust_decision.summary: Whether the dashboard's public port requires login is decided at startup by resolving a username/password pair from CLI flags and env vars into DashboardSettings.using_password; at the pinned commit only --flag and $ESPHOME_* are read, so an operator's pre-rename $USERNAME/$PASSWORD is ignored and auth silently turns off (the CLI mismatch guard resolves the same pair separately).

landing_point.why: DashboardSettings.parse_args is where ESPHOME_USERNAME/ESPHOME_PASSWORD are read and using_password is set, and its comment names the bare USERNAME/PASSWORD rename explicitly.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A lone OS-set $USERNAME must never be read as the dashboard username; CLI flags and $ESPHOME_* must still take precedence over the bare names.

O6_input_shapes: bare $USERNAME + $PASSWORD pair with no new-scheme credentials -> adopted
lone bare $PASSWORD -> mismatch error, not silent no-auth
bare var plus a half-set new scheme -> legacy not adopted, mismatch
candidate.O9_family: missing authentication via config/credential resolution (CWE-306, A07): a renamed env var silently fails open

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `or os.getenv('USERNAME')` / `or os.getenv('PASSWORD')` per credential in settings.parse_args only: this reads the OS $USERNAME on its own and leaves the CLI validator on the old rules.

out_of_scope_notes: The upstream fix reverses a documented design decision; the instruction states the required product behaviour so the tests are derivable from it.

sites: esphome_device_builder/__main__.py:467-474 (second resolver / mismatch guard; real upstream fix site)
routes: HTTP GET /devices on the dashboard port (device inventory)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a credential misconfiguration is refused by aborting startup; any non-zero exit that does not serve is accepted by design, so a crash and a clean refusal are indistinguishable at this contract level.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is the dashboard's own configuration and inventory as a whole; there is no per-resource authorization decision to aim at the wrong object.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: a single credential gate covers one role (dashboard client) and one direction (authentication); there are no roles or peer directions in this protection.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected surface in the task is read-only; no write route is introduced, so a reads-only guard cannot be distinguished from a correct one.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the credential values are compared verbatim; no normalisation, offset or clamp runs between configuration and the gate.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: there is no parsed identity object; a credential pair is present or absent, with no alternate spelling that could hide it.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no external authority to consult; the designed no-credentials mode is open and is covered by a positive functional test.
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the reference fix's shared resolver is additive; the alternative patch proves a second implementation, without a shared helper, also scores 1.0.
